subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

spec.name: Hover Technical
spec.description: A militarized pickup truck converted to ride on four ducted hover thrusters, in low-poly cyberpunk style with neon underglow, armor plating and a rear-mounted gun.
spec.layout: A chunky pickup silhouette hovering with its belly about 0.45 m above the floor. The front is +Z. The hood and armored grille sit at the front (z 1.2 to 2.7). The cab is in the middle (z -0.9 to 1.2), with a slanted windshield and a roof light bar. The open cargo bed sits behind the cab (z -2.7 to -0.9) and carries a pintle-mounted heavy gun. Four wheel-wells are replaced by ducted hover thrusters at the corners, each a drum with a glowing cyan core, hung from stub pylons. Nothing touches the floor except four small landing skids under the thrusters (y 0 to 0.12), so the floor parts are the running gear. Style: faceted slabs, chamfered boxes and hard colour blocks of gunmetal, olive-drab military paint with yellow hazard trim, plus cyan and magenta neon strips, decals (kanji-like glyphs, stencil numbers, hazard stripes) and glowing lights. Armor panels carry rivets and scuffed paint.

parts.builds: Hood, fenders and nose: a chamfered loft or slab hood sloping down to an armored grille. The grille is a dark plate with a painted vertical-slat texture, a glowing cyan slit visor and a magenta neon strip across the bumper. It also includes angled bull-bar tubes, twin headlights (lightWhite, glowing) in armored brow housings, a hood scoop with a hazard-stripe paint, rivet rows (panelled paint on hull), a stencil unit number decal on the hood, a front tow hook and a plated front skid. It also owns the front half of the lower chassis tub between z 0.9 and 2.7, with a neon underglow strip under the nose and the wheel-arch shaped cutouts above the thrusters, built as armor flares.
parts.attaches: Meets the cab at z 0.9 along the cabFloor and hoodTop line; the bumper sits at frontBumper; its flares cover the top of thrusterFL and thrusterFR without touching them.

parts.builds: The crew cab: a boxy armored cabin with a slanted windshield and side windows in dark glass with a glassGlow gradient texture, an armored roof with a cyan and magenta light bar, a roof antenna and sensor dome, and hazard stripe trim on the A-pillars. It also has two side doors with handles, slit armor shutters, riveted panels, side mirrors that are tiny camera pods, a decal with a glyph or kanji emblem and a faction badge on the doors, an exhaust-less rear window frame with a protective cage, and an interior hint of a dash, two seats and a steering wheel visible through the glass. It also owns the middle chassis tub between z -0.9 and 0.9, with side skirts carrying neon cyan strips.
parts.attaches: Sits on the cabFloor at y 0.75; its front meets the frontHull at z 0.9; its rear meets the cargoBed at z -0.95 with a rear-window cage bar.

parts.builds: The rear bed and tail: an open-topped bed with sloped armored side walls, an inner floor of corrugated plates with a painted rust and scuff texture, a tailgate with a hazard stripe and stencil text, a roll hoop with strap lights, and stacked cargo (ammo crates, a fuel drum, coiled cables). It also has two rear tail-light strips in lightRed that glow, a magenta neon underglow strip, a rear bumper and tow ring, and a central pintle-mounted heavy gun built in joints gunMount and gunBarrel: a swivel base, a shield plate with a slit and a glowing sight, a box magazine with a belt of rounds, a barrel with a perforated shroud and muzzle brake. Bed floor at y 0.85. Also owns the rear chassis tub between z -2.7 and -0.95.
parts.attaches: Starts at z -0.9 against the cabin rear. The gun base sits at gunPintle on bedFloor, riding gunMount and gunBarrel. Its rear flares cover the top of thrusterRL and thrusterRR without touching them.

parts.builds: All four hover thrusters and their mounts, as one reusable helper called per corner at mounts thrusterFL, thrusterFR, thrusterRL and thrusterRR, each riding its own joint. Each has a stub pylon arm connecting to the chassis underside at y 0.62, a wide drum nacelle (a lathe or octagonal cylinder, radius 0.42, height 0.34) in gunmetal with hazard stripes, an intake ring with a fan of angled blades, a glowing cyan core disc facing down with an emissive ring and inner magenta ring, downward exhaust vanes, small side warning lights, and a stenciled number. Each also has a short landing skid with a rubber foot, so the lowest points touch y = 0. Also adds the front-to-back underbody ducts with neon cyan edge lines and a faint translucent glow cone decal below each core.
parts.attaches: Each thruster is centred on its thrusterXX mount and joint. Pylons reach up to the underside of the chassis tubs at y 0.62 of frontHull, cabin and cargoBed.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to handle the Ctx type safely without conflicting with what the module already provides, deciding to avoid redeclaring it globally and instead use an inline type annotation when destructuring.

With that settled, I'm sketching the geometry for each thruster corner—placing the drum, skids, and connecting struts so they sit correctly relative to each other without overlapping, and planning a pylon slab to link the drum to the chassis underside. Then I start laying out the actual parts, beginning with a lathed drum shape and thinking about how to add hazard stripe paint along its surface.

Still writing lathe outline...

Still building thruster details...

Adding a light-shaft effect with crossed glowing cards near the floor, then planning front-to-back underbody ducts positioned at the chassis underside.

Now I'm sizing those duct boxes and thrusters relative to each other, then moving on to the paint palette, including hazard stripe bands and a drum paint function based on height along the lathe profile.

I'm working out joint and mount naming conventions for the thrusters, adding glow and bolt-head details around the rims, and tallying up the total part count across all the thruster assemblies to keep things reasonable—trimming bolt counts down to stay under budget.

I'm planning out a single buildCabin function, keeping it correct against the API while relying on the module's provided Ctx type rather than redeclaring it, and now I'm working out the coordinate setup.

I'm sketching out the cab geometry: a chassis tub, side skirts with cyan accent strips, a lower body box, and an extruded greenhouse profile for the slanted windshield and roof, planning the positions and thicknesses for each piece before adding side window panels.

For the windshield itself, I'm computing its slanted plane geometry—center position, length, and outward normal direction—so I can place a glass panel with a gradient texture slightly offset from the frame, along with pillar boxes to frame it.

Now I'm working out the side window geometry: placing glass planes at x=±1.16 with dimensions matching the slanted body profile, calculating the window's height and width so it fits between the front slope and the roofline.

For the interior, I'm considering whether seats and dashboard should peek through the glass — but since windows use opaque alpha-cut textures rather than true transparency, I may need to fake it by only rendering dark frame/trim patterns at the edges and leaving the rest implying glass without fully blocking the interior.

For dark tinted glass I'll draw the texture with gradient fills only in diagonal streak regions and a bottom band, leaving the rest transparent so the darkened cabin interior shows through. Then I'm laying out the tub as a gunmetal box with panel coloring, plus skirt boxes along the sides to close the underside.

Now I'm building the lower cab shell as a solid box so the cabin interior stays hidden below the window line, with seat cushions and backs positioned to peek above it and a dashboard placed near the windshield area.

For surface detail I'll use a panelled texture helper for door seams and rivets on the hull, treating it as paint rather than geometry since textures don't count toward part limits. Then I'm sketching door panels as thin boxes set into the side faces of the lower body.

Actual doors need handles and a rear window covered by slit armor shutters—I'm placing a plate with three thin dark slit boxes over the rear portion of the side window, with a plain window opening in front of it. I'm also planning a kanji emblem decal for the doors using an SVG texture.

Then I'm shaping the roof: an armored slab spanning the body width that chamfers down toward the windshield, topping out just under the height limit, plus a light bar with cyan elements mounted along the roof.

I'll cap the antenna at 2.1 to stay within the box, giving it a thin rod with a bulb tip. I'm also lowering the roof so the windshield top sits at 1.9, with the light bar at 1.9-2.0 and the sensor dome up to 2.02, then recalculating the windshield slope geometry from the greenhouse to the new roof height.

For the A-pillars, I'm placing angled rods on each side with hazard stripe coloring, working out the right sweep parameters and section shape to get flat-looking pillars rather than plain cylinders.

Now I'm laying out B and C pillars, the beltline rail, roof edge rail, and the rear window frame with its header and side slabs, figuring out the box dimensions and openings for each.

For the cage, I'm placing protective rods behind the rear window and adding the glass pane with a texture facing outward. On the sides, I'm defining the upper shutter plates with slit details, positioning them as thin proud boxes along the solid plate between the window opening and the lower body.

For the interior, I'm adding a dark hull-colored floor slab just above the cabin floor line to avoid z-fighting, plus a sloped dashboard panel with small glowing cyan instrument cluster planes.

Now I'm working out the steering wheel as a tilted torus positioned on the driver's side, connected to the dash by a column rod, and building box-based seats with cushions, backs, and headrests in gunmetal and rubber tones.

I'm skipping a rear bench to stick with just two seats, keeping the roof underside dark for the interior, and adding a sloped front brow/visor over the windshield for armored styling.

Now I'm setting precise roof dimensions — center y 1.92 with 0.08 thickness so the glass tucks underneath, then stacking the light bar and dome up to 2.06, with the antenna rod extending to 2.1. I'm also adding a paneling detail to the roof with armor plating and rivets.

Writing scuff shader function...

I also need the hull paint applied to armor doors, and I'm working out mirror camera pod placement—stalks extending from the box sides to small low-poly spheres with a forward-facing cyan lens glow, keeping them within the 2.6 width bound.

Now I'm placing hazard stripes on the A-pillar and door base, plus a door handle box positioned near the rear. For the door seam I'll skip extra outline boxes and just rely on a slightly proud panel with a dark rear edge box, then add a kanji-like glyph emblem on the door.

Working out positions for the badge circle and glyph so they don't overlap the handle, settling on the glyph centered lower and the badge offset toward the rear edge.

Sketching the glyph strokes...

I'll add diagonal gradient streaks to the glass texture for a reflective look, keeping it reusable across side windows, windshield, and rear glass by stretching the same texture rather than making separate ones. Then I'm positioning the windshield plane with its own orientation, size, and offset from the body surface.

For the side windows, I'm placing mirrored panes on each side with matching center height and width, checking they sit properly under the roofline and between the pillars. I'm also working out where to put B-pillar boxes and making sure the front pillar's slope lines up with the window's front edge at different heights.

There's still a gap below the window's front corner where the body would be open, so I'm adding a triangular fill piece to close that quarter-panel area, extruding a small outline along the x-axis mirrored to both sides.

For the rear pillars I'll use a similar approach. For the central tub, I'm sketching a chassis box positioned so its underside sits around y=0.5-0.62 to meet the pylons, possibly using two stacked boxes of different widths to suggest a chamfered shape.

Now I'm adding underglow details: a glowing cyan belly plate made of thin boxes near y=0.46, plus side skirt panels around x=±1.2 with a thin glowing strip, and small hazard trim caps at the ends.

I'm also planning the dashboard glow, interior dome light, dark cabin interior, and reusing the glow() helper for both solid and textured parts. Now I'm working on the light bar housing and lens strips—gunmetal box with cyan lens segments mounted on the front face.

Planning six alternating cyan/magenta strobe segments on the light bar, estimating around 120 total parts, then setting up helper functions for boxes and texture-mapped planes to keep the part-building code concise.

I'm settling on a limited color palette — gunmetal for seats, rubber for the wheel, rust accents — plus neon glow colors for the strobes, and defining a rod helper for the cage bars using point-to-point geometry.

For the hazard pillars I'm building a custom striped paint function that alternates between trim and gunmetal colors based on a diagonal sweep across y and z, using floored modulo math to keep the striping consistent even for negative values.

Now I'm placing the mirror stalk with a rod and a spherical pod housing a small glowing lens, then adding a hemispherical sensor dome with a steel base ring and glowing cyan accent near its mount point.

Still placing details... I'm adding an antenna assembly with a steel base cylinder, a thin rod, and a glowing magenta tip sphere, then moving on to constructing the seats as mirrored cushion and backrest boxes, tilting the backrests slightly for a reclined look.

I'm adjusting the headrest and backrest heights to avoid clipping through the roof, settling on a backrest around 1.37-1.79 and a headrest centered at 1.8, plus adding a rust seat stripe. Now I'm sketching the dashboard as a gunmetal box and starting on a hood-cowl hump above it.

Still placing dashboard elements...

Now adding console box between the seats, a tiny glowing roof lamp underside, and the rear wall structure with pillar framing around the window opening.

I'm sizing the header and sill pieces to close the opening top and bottom, then positioning the rear cage bars to meet the cargo bed edge, allowing a small overlap where the cage extends slightly past the body limit.

Now I'm placing the rear glass pane just behind the frame, then laying out the upper rear shutter plates with vertical slits, a B-pillar bar, and starting to define the roof's overall width and structure.

Still writing roof dimensions...

Still placing body panel details...

Skipping the roof stencil decal idea since it's risky, and moving on to writing the glass texture SVG with a gradient fill.

Still working out the wheel orientation facing the driver and the tub/body panel geometry, layering the bottom plate and underglow accents into the overall part composition.
